Entrance Exams After 12th — Complete Guide

Last updated: 2026-09-15

After Class 12, admission to many professional and university courses is decided through entrance exams. NTA (nta.ac.in) conducts major national exams like JEE Main, NEET UG and CUET UG, while CLAT is run separately by the law universities' consortium. Each exam has its own eligibility, syllabus and application window.

Simple explanation

JEE Main is the route to engineering seats in NITs, IIITs and many other institutions, and it is also the qualifying exam for JEE Advanced, which governs IIT admission. NEET UG is the single national entrance exam for MBBS and BDS seats. CUET UG is used by many central and participating universities for admission to their undergraduate programmes, including B.A., B.Sc., B.Com and others.

CLAT is the Common Law Admission Test used by the National Law Universities for their undergraduate law programmes; it is conducted by the Consortium of National Law Universities, not by NTA. On top of these, many states run their own engineering, medical or management entrance exams, and some colleges have their own entrance tests.

Each exam names its own qualifying condition: subject combination in Class 12 (for example PCM for most engineering routes and PCB for medical), age requirements, and nationality or domicile rules where applicable. You must check the notification for the specific year you are applying in.

Why does it matter?

Which exam you take decides which colleges and courses you are eligible for, the syllabus you prepare for, and the application budget and calendar you plan around. Applying to the correct exam for your target course avoids wasting a year and keeps your options open across institutions.

Example

In numbers

A Class 12 science student aiming for a B.Tech seat at an NIT would register for JEE Main, prepare from the syllabus shared in the JEE Main information bulletin, appear in the session(s) notified, and then use the score to participate in counselling. A student aiming for MBBS would instead register for NEET UG, since NEET is the required national exam for that route.

Major exams and what they lead to

JEE Main leads to B.E./B.Tech admissions at NITs, IIITs and other participating institutes, and also qualifies candidates for JEE Advanced for IIT seats. NEET UG leads to MBBS and BDS seats in government and private medical colleges. CUET UG is used for undergraduate admission in central and participating universities across a wide range of programmes. CLAT leads to B.A. LL.B. and other law programmes at National Law Universities.

Do not mix up exam names: JEE Main and JEE Advanced are linked but separate, and CLAT is separate from NTA exams. Confirm the official body for the exam before trusting any third-party updates.

Eligibility and dates

Eligibility is set in each exam's official information bulletin. Common points: Class 12 with the required subjects, minimum marks in Class 12 for some routes, upper or lower age limits for exams like NEET, and Indian nationality or eligibility as notified. JEE Main is held in multiple sessions through the academic year, while NEET UG and CUET UG are typically held once a year in a notified window.

Exam dates, session announcements, and application start and end dates are published on the official portals (nta.ac.in, jeemain.nta.nic.in, neet.nta.nic.in, cuet.nta.nic.in, and consortiumofnlus.ac.in for CLAT). Always read the current year's information bulletin; previous year's dates do not guarantee the same calendar.

Preparation

Start from the official syllabus and previous years' papers, keep the board textbooks as base for science subjects, and take full-length timed mock tests. For CUET, focus on the subjects you actually select in the exam rather than attempting every possible section.

Build a realistic schedule: complete the syllabus once, then revise through mocks and analyse mistakes. Avoid the trap of collecting many paid materials before finishing the official syllabus.

Application process

The application is online on the official portal. Register with your details and the specified photograph and signature, fill the form, pay the application fee, and download the confirmation page. Later you download the admit card (hall ticket) with your exam centre before the exam date.

Read the information bulletin point by point — the syllabus, marking scheme and admissible documents for exam day are all listed there. Discrepancies in your name, date of birth or category between the application and your certificates are a common cause of trouble at the exam centre and at counselling.

Advertisement

Important things to know

  • Apply only through the official exam portal for the exam you are targeting.
  • Keep your photograph, signature and category details consistent with your documents.
  • Download and read the current year's information bulletin before applying.
  • The admit card is mandatory at the examination centre; print it as directed.
  • Syllabus and pattern changes are notified officially — do not rely on coaching-market rumours.

Common mistakes

  • Preparing for the wrong syllabus, for example mixing JEE Main and NEET patterns.
  • Submitting documents with mismatched spellings or dates compared with your certificates.
  • Missing the application window, then paying private agencies for 'late' applications.
  • Ignoring the marking scheme and negative marking rules.
  • Not checking the exam-city intimation or the correct session in multi-session exams.

Frequently asked questions

Which entrance exam should I take for engineering?

For NIT, IIIT and many state or private institutes, register for JEE Main; those who qualify may attempt JEE Advanced for IIT seats. Check participating institutes in the current bulletin.

Is NEET UG the only exam for MBBS?

NEET UG is the national exam used for MBBS and BDS admissions in India. Verify the current rules and participating colleges in the official bulletin.

Does NTA conduct CLAT?

No. CLAT is conducted by the Consortium of National Law Universities through its own website (consortiumofnlus.ac.in). NTA conducts JEE Main, NEET UG, CUET UG and other notified exams.

Can I apply for both JEE Main and CUET UG?

Yes, if you meet each exam's eligibility. They are separate exams for different institutions, so applying to both keeps more options open, but fees and preparation are separate.

When are applications and exams held?

Windows are announced each year on the official portals. There is no fixed month guaranteed every year — always check the current information bulletin.

What documents do I need on exam day?

The admit card printout and a valid ID (such as Aadhaar, school ID or passport) matching the details on the admit card, as stated in the current bulletin.
